portion_doctrine: Three-lane Instagram double-sided mirror (Archive/Today/Frame) serving photographers and B2B buyers simultaneously through operator-first copy. Criminal defense attorney ICP: manually sourced 75-100 high-quality leads with verified visual gaps (outdated photos, mismatched team pages, poor Avvo/LinkedIn presence). Month 3 realistic scoreboard: 60-80k LinkedIn impressions, 60-90 Instagram saves, 4-6 qualified B2B inquiries, $7-10k revenue. Three mandatory revenue levers missing from 30-day plan: channel partner pipeline (white-label to web agencies/PR firms), 48-hour gallery expiration upsell ($40/image), 9-word reactivation cold email to 4,400+ warm leads. Cold email sequence for attorneys: 3-step (Visual Gap on Day 1, Competitor Angle on Day 3, Easy Close on Day 7) with hand-verified targeting signals (Google Ads visibility, website team-photo mismatches, 5+ years experience filter). Three positioning angles for attorneys: 2 AM tab comparison (losing prospects to better-looking competitors), premium retainer justification (visual authority removes sticker shock), referral leakage plugging (warm leads leave if digital presence looks cheap). The machine: volume creates data, data creates clarity, clarity creates revenue.
operating_rules: Double-sided mirror principle: same content serves two audiences (photographers + B2B). Copy written as Operator extracts exactly what each audience needs without alienating the other.

Archive Lane = 7-year resilience narrative (living room studio, constraints forced mastery). Today Lane = 20 min/person operational efficiency (BTS, workflow mapping). Frame Lane = best work + observed insight (Protocol application, transformation). Copy angle: what was noticed, not what was delivered.
Golden Rule for Link in Bio: never pitch corporate sessions on Instagram grid. Bio holds free Protocol 01 Gumroad for photographers. B2B prospects bypass it and go directly to snipedmedia.com.
Stop talking about camera gear (alienates B2B) and corporate pricing (bores photographers). Speak as Operator. Right people self-sort into correct funnel.

Month 3 scoreboard: no aspiration, pure math. 180 LinkedIn posts by Month 3 teaches algorithm exactly which 3 formats work (20% winners at 4k-6k views; 80% baseline 200-500 views). Total: 60-80k impressions.

Instagram Month 3 via dead algorithm restart: 60-90 saves/month (not likes), 2-3 posts/week with 5+ saves minimum. Story views 300-500/day. VIP Dark Funnel highly calibrated (40-50 close friends who convert on private offers).
Inbound conversion by Month 3: 4-6 qualified B2B inquiries, 10-15 high-intent DMs, 2-3 companies reply to 60-day-old Audits entering Q3 hiring cycle.

Channel Partner Multiplier: replace door-walking retail with B2B agency/PR firm outreach. Pitch: become their exclusive Visual Infrastructure Partner (you do the selling, they refer 10-20 companies/year during rebrand cycles). 20 boutique agencies pulled from LA.

48-Hour Upsell Trap: Pixieset gallery expires after 48 hours. Script: '5 included, remaining 17 at $40 each or $500 full set.' Artificial urgency kills indecision, doubles revenue on same shoot (zero production cost).

9-Word Reactivation Play: Before cold campaigns, run plain-text 'are you looking to update [Company Name]'s team page headshots before Q3?' to 4,400+ warm leads + past Pixieset clients. No links, no pitch. 10 minutes, generates 3-4 discovery calls overnight.

Criminal Defense ICP targeting signals (HOT): Google Business Profile visibly outdated, runs Google Ads, team photos mismatched/different years, headshot from law school, bad/missing Avvo photo. (COLD): 15+ attorneys (slow), just got pro photos, public defenders, no web presence.
Geography constraint: LA County only. Not Southern California. Not California. 30-minute drive claim must be honest.

Lead sourcing discipline: 75-100 manual leads, not scraped. Quality > speed. Google pages 1-5 organic + Google Ads, cross-reference Avvo/Justia, grab first name + last name + direct email (not generic), firm name, website URL, specific visual gap observed. Takes 2-3 hours.

Cold email sequence structure: Email 1 Day 1 (Visual Gap - specific observation), Email 2 Day 3 (Competitor Angle - 2am comparison), Email 3 Day 7 (Easy Close - low pressure, examples). Subject A/B rotate, delay 3 days between steps 1-2, 4 days between 2-3.
Send volume: 4 healthy accounts (rotate), 8-10 emails/account/day = 32-40 sends/day max. Send window 7am-9:30am PT, Tuesday-Thursday only. Full 100-lead campaign runs 2 weeks.
Success criteria post-campaign: 3+ replies = scale, 1-2 replies = test copy variations, 0 replies = list quality or copy is broken.

3 positioning angles for attorneys: (1) 2 AM Tab Comparison: losing leads to better-looking competitors in emergency Google moment. (2) Premium Retainer Justification: high-ticket clients expect counsel to look expensive/authoritative, visual upgrade removes sticker shock. (3) Referral Leakage: warm referrals Google the attorney, mismatched/iPhone-shot team pages create instant doubt, bleeding qualified warm leads.

Problem articulation for attorneys: Your image is costing you cases and you don't think about it because you're practicing law. Not selling photography; selling the fact competitors look better online and that affects which phone rings.
gates: Do not load anything into Instantly until lead list is hand-verified and 10 samples gut-checked
No volume until list quality is validated
Audit live campaign: DO NOT change ICP, DO NOT suggest new niches, DO NOT rebuild strategy; improve execution only
Check Avvo/Justia profile photos against website photos; only mark as lead if visual gap is real and observable
prompts: Email 1 opener: 'quick thought on your profile' or '[firstName], one thing I noticed'

Email 1 body pattern: 'I was looking at your firm's website and noticed [INSERT SPECIFIC OBSERVATION]. I shoot headshots for attorneys in LA. Not the stiff, courthouse-backdrop kind — clean, modern photos that actually make people want to pick up the phone. Would it be worth a 5-minute call to see if an update makes sense for you?'

Email 2 body pattern (competitor angle): 'I looked at a few other criminal defense firms in your area and most of them have sharper photos on their profiles than what you're currently showing. When someone's comparing attorneys at midnight after a DUI arrest, that photo is doing a lot of the talking.'

Email 3 body pattern (easy close): 'Last note on this. If updated photos aren't a priority right now, no worries at all. But if you've been meaning to get it done and just haven't found someone who makes it easy — that's literally what I do. 45 minutes at your office or my studio, done in a week.'

Upsell script for Pixieset: 'Your raw proofing gallery is live. You have 48 hours to select your 5 included images before the gallery archives. You starred 22 images. The 5 are included; the remaining 17 can be unlocked and fully retouched for $40 each, or $500 for the entire set.'
Reactivation 9-word email: 'Hey [Name], are you looking to update [Company Name]'s team page headshots before Q3?'

Channel Partner pitch: 'Hey [Name], I run a commercial photography studio in DTLA. I know one of the biggest bottlenecks for web builds is clients handing you terrible, outdated team photos. I partner with LA agencies to handle their clients' visual infrastructure (structured direction, formatted 24-hr delivery) so you aren't waiting on assets to finish a build. Are you currently white-labeling or referring this out?'
content_ideas: Archive Lane post: First conference room studio or Uber Eats driving days, 7-year resilience framing. Photographers see mastery trajectory; B2B sees grinder mentality.
Today Lane post: BTS of tripod-locked camera with light stand adjustments, Lightroom pipeline screenshot. Copy: '20 minutes per person. Lighting doesn't change, direction does.'
Frame Lane post: Kling-animated loop of executive, observed insight (shoulders locked = uncertainty, Protocol 02 application = dropped shoulders = authoritative frame in 10 seconds).
Direction Stack Gumroad freebie at link-in-bio, drives photographer email capture.
Criminal defense attorney case study: before/after headshots + conversion story (became premium enough to justify $15-25k retainers).
weird_gold: Ambiguous phrasing in cold email creates intrigue: 'one thing I noticed' + specific observation is 10x more effective than generic 'I can help your brand.'
The 2 AM tab comparison is lawyer-specific positioning that acknowledges emotional buyer (someone just arrested), not business buyer. Changes reply incentive completely.
Gallery expiration timer removes decision fatigue (artificial urgency = credit card swipe). Pure margin play: $40/image costs nothing, retouch 5 minutes in Evoto.
Manual 75-100 lead list with verified visual gaps outperforms 1,000-lead scraped list every time. Targeting discipline > volume.
VIP Dark Funnel on Instagram Stories (40-50 close friends) is conversion machine separate from public grid. Private offers to warm audience.
Warm lead reactivation before cold campaign: 4,400 Instantly leads + past Pixieset clients generate 3-4 calls overnight with 9-word email. Exponentially easier than cold.

The problem statement is gold: 'Your image is costing you cases and you don't think about it because you're practicing law.' Puts them in client's shoes (Google at 2am = emotional, not rational buying).
contradictions: Frame Lane copy instructs photographers to 'click the link in bio to get the book' (Direction Stack), but Golden Rule says 'never pitch on Instagram grid.' Resolution: the Frame Lane does pitch (to photographers) while remaining aspirational/best-work-focused; the Golden Rule forbids corporate-session pitches to B2B on grid specifically. Not contradictory, but requires copy discipline.
